findings.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:~969 — Test 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry' does not exercise the denial-cache path: the permCache entry is set to false (deny) even though the comment says 'Allow access ... to prove this is not checked', and the request sets Folder='fold1' while the lookup key is built from checkReq.ParentFolder (empty), so the pre-populated key '..._dash1_fold1' never matches the computed key '..._dash1_'. The test passes whether or not the denial-cache code works. Set the permCache value to true, populate ParentFolder (or key on Folder), and assert the store was not called.

[Medium/performance] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:124-142 — When the permission cache hits but the result is 'deny', Check falls through to getIdentityPermissions, which after this PR always fetches from the store (permCache reads were removed from getUserPermissions/getAnonymousPermissions). Previously a perm-cache hit answered denials with zero DB access; now every distinct denied resource triggers a full permission query once per shortCacheTTL window (the denial cache only dedupes repeats of the same resource), amplifying DB load from per-(user,action) to per-(user,action,resource) for deny-heavy traffic (browsing/scanning inaccessible resources, anonymous users, etc.).

[Medium/performance] pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:101 — The in-process client's 30s response cache is replaced with NoopCache, but the new server-side cache explicitly excludes TypeRenderService (getCachedIdentityPermissions returns cache.ErrNotFound for it), so render-service checks now hit the permission store on every call with no caching at any layer. The remote client path (newRemoteRBACClient) retains its client-side cache, so the two deployment paths behave inconsistently.

[Low/bug] pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:30 — The denial key omits checkReq.Folder, which checkPermission's scope matching takes into account (folder-scoped grants). A denial cached from a request with one Folder value (or none) will deny later requests for the same resource name with a different Folder (e.g., after a dashboard is moved, or a caller omitting the folder hint) until the TTL expires — fail-closed, but produces false denials.

[Low/data] pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:30 — Key fields are joined with '_', which is a legal character in Grafana UIDs, so distinct (name, parent) pairs can collide (e.g., name='a_b', parent='c' vs name='a', parent='b_c'), making a denial cached for one resource deny a different resource. Use a separator that cannot occur in the components or length-prefix the fields.

[Low/bug] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:118,138 — permissionCacheUsage is miscounted: a denial-cache hit increments the permission-cache 'true' label (a different cache), and a permission-cache hit whose check returns false (the stale-cache fallback path) is counted as 'false'/miss even though the cache was hit. This distorts the cache hit-rate signal this PR introduces.

[Low/bug] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:342 — getCachedIdentityPermissions swallows every error, not just cache misses (e.g., store errors from GetUserIdentifiers, or the unsupported-identity-type error), with no logging, and the caller then repeats the same failing work in the fallback path. Only cache.ErrNotFound should be treated as a fallthrough condition; other errors should at least be logged.

goldens.comment: The Check operation exhibits asymmetric cache trust logic: cached permission grants are trusted and returned immediately, but cached denials from the same permission cache are ignored, leading to a fresh database lookup. This allows stale cached grants to provide access to revoked resources, posing a security risk.
The test comment says the cached permissions 'allow access', but the map stores false for dashboards:uid:dash1, so checkPermission will still treat this scope as not allowed.

The cache key construction in `userPermDenialCacheKey` uses simple string concatenation with underscores, which can lead to ambiguous keys and collision risks when any component contains underscores or is empty. This could result in incorrect denial cache hits, affecting user permissions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/performance] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:124-142 — When the permission cache hits but the result is 'deny', Check falls through to getIdentityPermissions, which after this PR always fetches from the store (permCache reads were removed from getUserPermissions/getAnonymousPermissions). Previously a perm-cache hit answered denials with zero DB access; now every distinct denied resource triggers a full permission query once per shortCacheTTL window (the denial cache only dedupes repeats of the same resource), amplifying DB load from per-(user,action) to per-(user,action,resource) for deny-heavy traffic (browsing/scanning inaccessible resources, anonymous users, etc.).

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Check` now tries `getCachedIdentityPermissions(...)` first and only returns early on cached *allow* (service.go:113-142). If the cache is present but `checkPermission` returns `allowed == false`, it falls through to `getIdentityPermissions(...)`, which ultimately calls `getUserPermissions`/`getAnonymousPermissions`. In this PR, the direct `permCache.Get(...)` fast-path reads were removed from both `getUserPermissions` and `getAnonymousPermissions` (service.go:377-421 and 421+), so that fallthrough will hit the store (modulo singleflight) even when the (user,action) permission map was already cached. The new `permDenialCache` only short-circuits repeated denials for the exact (user,action,name,parent) key, so deny-heavy traffic can increase DB load compared to the prior behavior. This is a performance/behavior tradeoff rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/performance] pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:101 — The in-process client's 30s response cache is replaced with NoopCache, but the new server-side cache explicitly excludes TypeRenderService (getCachedIdentityPermissions returns cache.ErrNotFound for it), so render-service checks now hit the permission store on every call with no caching at any layer. The remote client path (newRemoteRBACClient) retains its client-side cache, so the two deployment paths behave inconsistently.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly disables the authzlib client-side cache for the in-process path by wiring `authzlib.WithCacheClientOption(&NoopCache{})` in `ProvideAuthZClient` (rbac.go), while `newRemoteRBACClient` still constructs an authzlib client with `cache.NewLocalCache(...)`, so the two deployment paths now have inconsistent caching behavior. It’s also true that the new server-side cache helper `getCachedIdentityPermissions` explicitly bypasses caching for `types.TypeRenderService` by returning `cache.ErrNotFound`, meaning render-service requests won’t benefit from the newly added server-side cache checks (though the claim that it *necessarily* hits the permission store on every call can’t be fully proven from the shown diff alone). This is a concrete performance/architecture concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the denial cache key explicitly includes the folder/parent folder value: `userPermDenialCacheKey(namespace, userUID, action, name, parent)` appends both `name` and `parent`, and `Check` computes it as `userPermDenialCacheKey(..., checkReq.Name, checkReq.ParentFolder)`. The new test also sets/uses a key including the folder (`..., "dash1", "fold1"`) while passing `Folder: "fold1"` in the request, confirming folder is part of the denial key in this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:118,138 — permissionCacheUsage is miscounted: a denial-cache hit increments the permission-cache 'true' label (a different cache), and a permission-cache hit whose check returns false (the stale-cache fallback path) is counted as 'false'/miss even though the cache was hit. This distorts the cache hit-rate signal this PR introduces.

adjudication.rationale: In Service.Check, a permDenialCache hit (permDenialCache.Get) increments permissionCacheUsage with label "true" (service.go around the new early-return), even though that is not a permission-cache hit but a separate denial cache. Also, when getCachedIdentityPermissions returns cachedPerms (cache hit) but checkPermission returns allowed==false, the code falls through and increments permissionCacheUsage with label "false" before fetching from DB, so cache-hit-but-stale/insufficient entries are counted as misses. Both behaviors are directly shown in the added logic and will distort the intended cache hit-rate metric.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:342 — getCachedIdentityPermissions swallows every error, not just cache misses (e.g., store errors from GetUserIdentifiers, or the unsupported-identity-type error), with no logging, and the caller then repeats the same failing work in the fallback path. Only cache.ErrNotFound should be treated as a fallthrough condition; other errors should at least be logged.

adjudication.rationale: In both Check and List, the code treats *any* error from getCachedIdentityPermissions as a cache-miss and falls back (e.g., `cachedPerms, err := ...; if err == nil { ... }` else go to `getIdentityPermissions`). But getCachedIdentityPermissions can return non-cache-miss errors (e.g., from `s.GetUserIdentifiers(...)` or `fmt.Errorf("unsupported identity type")`). Those errors are not surfaced/logged at the cache lookup site and can cause duplicated failing work in the fallback path (GetUserIdentifiers again). However, the error is typically still returned/logged later when getIdentityPermissions fails, so it’s more of an inefficiency/diagnostics issue than a clear functional defect.
